title: Study of Ferroelectric Phases in HfZrOx Thin Films with Varying La Content Using Precession Electron Diffraction & In-Situ Heating- Biasing Techniques
content: Recently La-doped Hafnium Zirconate (HZO) thin films have attracted enormous research interest in semiconductor industries as a promising candidate material for micro capacitor, non-volatile ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM), ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) and ferroelectric tunnel junction (FTJ) applications[1-4]. The HZO exists most abundantly in three allotropes, namely orthorhombic (o-phase, Pca21), tetragonal (t-phase, P42/nmc) and monoclinic (m-phase, P21/c), which are affected by various factors such as dopants, impurities, and stress/strain. The non-centrosymmetric o-phase exhibits ferroelectric behavior whereas the t-phase is anti-ferroelectric and metastable. Monoclinic phase is the most stable phase; however, it is non-ferroelectric in nature. Therefore, achieving a predominantly ferroelectric o-phase is critical for industrial applications in the memory-electronic field [5]. The o/t/m-phase fraction in HZO can be tailored by the La dopant content, by forming oxygen vacancies in the HZO layer [3, 4, 6]. The antiferroelectric tetragonal phase can transform into the ferroelectric orthorhombic phase upon biasing, however upon thermal annealing at higher temperature (>800°C) it transforms into the stable m-phase, which lacks ferroelectric properties [3-6].
